answer: Persistent work-history receipts. Each identity accumulates a public ledger of completed tasks, and rewards unlock only after a delay that resets on any duplicate claim from the same operator. At dawn each cycle, payouts clear against that ledger. An attacker cloning identities must independently complete enough real work on each clone to cross the knoll of eligibility before rewards release, so costs scale with the number of clones rather than staying flat. Clones that wander without work earn nothing, and faking history requires matching real task outputs.
